solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film fan Harry came in with vamp

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive, promiscuous woman, which old slang calls a goer

explanation.surface: A movie fan is pestered by a seductive woman who has come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' means harass, signalling the anagram; 'vamp' is old slang for a flirtatious, promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who regularly attends films at the pictures is a film fan.

clue.text: Change when chief comes round

indicators.note: the abbreviation for chief encircles the other word, so it comes round it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Things alter whenever the boss comes back to his senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Change is loose coins, a form of ready money.

clue.text: Champion, reckless, lacking length with racket

parts.note: a champion is number one, written NO I

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the synonym for reckless

parts.note: silly can mean foolishly reckless

explanation.surface: A careless champion who has lost his reach plays with his tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like a tennis bat but means din; I in NO I is the Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with a racket means making a great deal of din, which is acting loudly.

clue.text: Very appetising argument and how it turned out

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are turned inside out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A row breaks out and we learn how it ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Food so tempting it makes saliva flow is described as very appetising.

clue.text: Guardian's leader shone light on church failing

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to shine light on something is to light it up, past tense lit

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial exposed the church's shortcomings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' plays on a newspaper editorial, but here it only takes the first letter of Guardian's.
explanation.definitionFit: A failing in the sense of a fault or malfunction is a technical hitch.

clue.text: Plant nuts with pine fruit, about 100

parts.note: in printing an en is also called a nut, so nuts are ens

indicators.note: about means the fruit's letters go around the number's

parts.note: the fruit of a pine tree is a cone
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: set out nuts with pine cones, roughly a hundred of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' is printers' jargon: an en space is called a nut, so nuts gives ENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant oneself somewhere comfortable and secure is to settle in snugly.

clue.text: Party's withdrawn Murphy

indicators.note: withdrawn suggests drawing back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party; with the 's it gives DUPS

explanation.surface: A political party has expelled a man named Murphy.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy looks like a surname, but it is Irish-flavoured slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy and its synonym are both informal names for a potato.

clue.text: Sage's quiet place to hide boring routine

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
a den is a lair or hideaway

explanation.surface: A wise man finds a quiet hideaway to escape a dull routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage as an adjective means wise and judicious, showing good sense.

clue.text: Fair treatment expected for tax

parts.note: something due is expected, as in a train due at noon
pro means for, in favour of
a cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: Anyone expecting a tax bill wants to be treated fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase means fair procedure guaranteed by law to every person.

clue.text: Spurs stumped by short cross between pair

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: between means the shortened word sits inside the pair

parts.note: II is the Roman numeral for two

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Tottenham, baffled by a brief cross between two of their players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spurs' looks like Tottenham Hotspur football club but is a plural noun meaning incentives.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurs are things that prompt action, the same as incentives or prompts.

clue.text: Charge forces American to block petition

indicators.note: to block means to sit in the middle of the other word, stopping it up

parts.note: to sue is to petition or appeal
F is an abbreviation for force, so two forces are FF

explanation.surface: Police charge armed forces, with an American trying to stop a petition.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge something with a quality is to fill or spread through it.

clue.text: Ogle briefs dancing 'ere?

indicators.note: dancing letters are moved about into a new arrangement

parts.note: a dropped-aitch rendering of here, giving its three letters

explanation.surface: A cockney asks if this is where you watch knickers on the dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the Paris music hall famous for scantily clad dancers is where one might ogle briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris cabaret is renowned for revues of dancers in skimpy costumes.

clue.text: Where to study hip after trips round hospital

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: drug trips are highs

indicators.note: round means the word for hip goes around the hospital's letter

parts.note: hip and cool both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A hip injured on trips round the hospital needs study.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary school for teenagers is a place where pupils learn.

clue.text: Removing odd bits, repair organ

indicators.note: removing the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A surgeon fixes an organ by cutting away the odd bits.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing is a body part, so an organ by example.

clue.text: Main explorer's occupation in delta avoiding work clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the outer word dresses the inner ones

parts.note: skiving is British slang for dodging work
Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An explorer in a river delta shirks work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, and 'clothes' is a verb meaning wraps around, not garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exploring the sea underwater spends time swimming beneath its surface.

clue.text: Part of remote island home?

parts.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys
pad is slang for one's home

explanation.surface: A house on a far-flung island is pictured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' reads as far away but is a television remote control.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote control has a panel of buttons, a numbered button panel.

clue.text: Catholic European clubs shown round Celtic ground

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Visiting European football clubs are given a tour of Celtic's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic is a Glasgow football club; 'Catholic' is not the religion but the lower-case sense of wide-ranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic tastes are broad and wide-ranging, drawn from many sources.

clue.text: Note key concealed in throw under the counter

indicators.note: concealed in means these pieces are hidden inside the word for throw

parts.note: to shy is to toss or throw
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A note with a key is hidden in a throw for an illicit deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Under-the-counter deals are furtive and secret, done covertly.

clue.text: Slick English touring Oz are repellent

indicators.note: touring means going around, so these letters surround the country

parts.note: slick and neat both mean deft and tidy
Oz is slang for Australia, abbreviated AUS

explanation.surface: The smooth English cricketers touring Australia are thoroughly disliked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works as a plural verb: things that are repellent sicken people.
explanation.definitionFit: To be repellent is to sicken or disgust those who encounter it.

clue.text: Device that's universal able to be drawn out briefly

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: tensile means capable of being stretched or drawn out

explanation.surface: A universal gadget that briefly extends.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool or implement is a device for a practical task.

clue.text: Try to seize old superior westbound vessels

indicators.note: in an across entry westbound means read right to left
to seize means the word for try holds the other letter inside

parts.note: to have a stab is to have a try
U stands for upper-class or superior

explanation.surface: Someone tries to seize old superior ships heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: German submarines of the World Wars were naval vessels.

clue.text: Draw a short line separating tees

indicators.note: separating means the shortened word sits between the two letters, keeping them apart

parts.note: tees are the letter T twice

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a railway line is a track

explanation.surface: On a golf course, draw a short line between the tees.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to pull or lure people in.

clue.text: Light lead-free fuel

indicators.note: lead-free means the word loses its leading letter

parts.note: lignite is brown coal, a fuel

explanation.surface: Light up with unleaded petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire is to set it burning, to kindle it.

clue.text: Anger republic ceding territory

indicators.note: ceding means giving up, so a stretch of letters is removed

parts.note: Ireland is a republic
land is territory

explanation.surface: There is fury that a republic is surrendering territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger and its synonym both mean wrath or fury.

clue.text: I argue with aunt manoeuvring launch

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: I quarrel with my aunt, manoeuvring the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a scheme is to formally begin or open it.

clue.text: The Times abandoning superior booze

indicators.note: abandoning means the letters are dropped from the word for superior

parts.note: better means superior
T stands for time, so times are two Ts

explanation.surface: The newspaper gives up superior drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the newspaper setting the puzzle, but it is just T for time, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink, of which ale is an example.

clue.text: Being visible, I succeeded during evening

indicators.note: during means the letter falls within the word for evening

parts.note: night and evening both mean the dark hours
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: I triumphed one evening and was seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within view is able to be seen, so visible.

clue.text: Bookish learner's going to do repeats

indicators.note: going means the learner's letter departs from the word

parts.note: literate means well-read, bookish
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A studious learner is going to repeat a year.
explanation.definitionFit: To do repeats is to go over the same thing again and again.

clue.text: In future, litter producer's self-reproach picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: guilt is self-reproach

explanation.surface: Someone who litters will later feel guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: A young sow that has not yet farrowed is the future producer of a litter of piglets.
explanation.definitionFit: A young female pig that will one day have piglets is a future litter producer.

clue.text: Kind dog, one no longer seen in Fleet Street

definitions.text: one no longer seen in Fleet Street

parts.note: kind and type both mean sort
a setter is a gun dog breed

explanation.surface: A friendly dog that has disappeared from a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street was London's newspaper district; the papers moved out and hot-metal typesetting vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: Compositors who set metal type for newspapers vanished from Fleet Street with computerisation.
